ICPSR Summer Workshop, "Sensitivity
Analysis: Quantifying the Robustness of Inferences to Alternative Factors or
Data <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/umich-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/22KJvC2mY7Gra2NcCv-gUl7mufrnbCzcIUBTd3rUYsG-5Sov7jgFrZnOBOMkAKgVVGrIfCprFvMT0of_-h7-HEupzLWKoUqBhDEh7X5ixua9e2xxJ-bWch5aI9kyVl_hQNiB0lhTQntfc7uAsfauTQbjJi2TbiGjZqv9s4zmLHPHmqPuC__;!!HXCxUKc!3S3tXZMTsU1cP7ePkMICgdlS4MeejSXf8A4BQI6zj0wi83pqhv0Vdj2wUwGl_wHv6WXtd5URIIp0GkXSADU$>," July 8-12, 2024. Hybrid (virtual, FtF in Ann Arbor, MI, with
asynchronous access to materials).

Most social scientists need to consider the unobserved
conditions that could change an inference. This workshop is about the
statistical tools (R,  Stata or the konfound-it app <https://konfound-project.shinyapps.io/konfound-it/>)
to do just that, quantifying the strength of evidence to inform policy,
practice, or general social science.

This workshop is a full 20 instruction hours
elaborating on the Mar 21 talk “Sensitivity Analysis for Quantifying the
Robustness of Causal Inference” given by Ken Frank <https://education.msu.edu/people/frank-kenneth/>.

Go here to register <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/umich-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/2xSc-y_ytf03yTwxHV1PTUd5gIu9CbqU4EFhexiF9QOq9Sov7jgGxjfUBcL4GUEwN753fOzVj8Akf7efB07AmJfFho-IYgRsFc8NMVUpehSfprHVgHICUWFVhrSD4y2t8KfOduYW8jyTYoqmi0Tej9dx4ztUdwSmEUMyN5bqAiF_1i7efjr7YRtGb7JfYkhCUrfTdwHdcdFXuiQay7t4t-OE-EvKzIJHEDB0TMOdEJrQWZ0u_v4SA70s5UTP3nNIaNdn39E6Ge6U_NSbLJ7w310t874zVeg__;!!HXCxUKc!3S3tXZMTsU1cP7ePkMICgdlS4MeejSXf8A4BQI6zj0wi83pqhv0Vdj2wUwGl_wHv6WXtd5URIIp0uyWIQ7k$>. Group discounts <https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/pages/sumprog/registration.html#:~:text=Discount%20for%20Returning%20ICPSR%20Summer,this%20year&> available as well.

messages.body_plain:
[The links below may be a little
quicker.]

Hope you are doing
well. I thought you might be interested in the below.  Please feel free to
share widely.

Space is still
available to register <https://web.cvent.com/event/6a962cf4-05e7-45fb-8f6f-eafe8c67ce53/regPage:1355f491-6480-4e9b-bc3d-8974da6b0ace>
for the hybrid (virtual or FtF, asynchronous access to materials) ICPSR Summer
Course, "Sensitivity Analysis: Quantifying the Robustness of Inferences
to Alternative Factors or Data <https://myumi.ch/N61ER>", July 8-12, 2024.

Most social
scientists need to consider the unobserved conditions that could change an
inference. This workshop is about the statistical tools (R,  Stata or the konfound-it app <https://konfound-project.shinyapps.io/konfound-it/>)
to do just that, quantifying the strength of evidence to inform policy,
practice, or general social science.

It’s 20
instruction hours -- half a semester's worth of instruction in just 5
days. That gives us time to tailor to specific examples or approaches in your
field.

Group discounts <https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/pages/sumprog/registration.html#:~:text=Discount%20for%20Returning%20ICPSR%20Summer,this%20year&>
available as well.

Ken
